Davis R M Inc. Sells 15,459 Shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) Posted by Paula Ricardo | Apr 25th, 2018
Davis R M Inc. cut its holdings in Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 3.3% during the fourth quarter, according to its most recent Form 13F filing with the SEC. The fund owned 450,248 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 15,459 shares during the period. Apple accounts for about 3.0% of Davis R M Inc.’s portfolio, making the stock its largest holding. Davis R M Inc.’s holdings in Apple were worth $76,195,000 at the end of the most recent quarter.
Other institutional investors and hedge funds have also added to or reduced their stakes in the company. Beach Investment Management LLC. boosted its stake in Apple by 1,517.7% in the second quarter. Beach Investment Management LLC. now owns 178,109 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $25,651,000 after acquiring an additional 167,099 shares in the last quarter. Catalyst Capital Advisors LLC boosted its stake in Apple by 39.8% in the second quarter. Catalyst Capital Advisors LLC now owns 69,900 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $10,067,000 after acquiring an additional 19,900 shares in the last quarter. IFC Holdings Incorporated FL boosted its stake in Apple by 1.1% in the second quarter. IFC Holdings Incorporated FL now owns 85,072 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $12,224,000 after acquiring an additional 885 shares in the last quarter. Wedbush Securities Inc. boosted its stake in Apple by 3.6% in the second quarter. Wedbush Securities Inc. now owns 156,649 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $22,561,000 after acquiring an additional 5,435 shares in the last quarter. Finally, Berkeley Capital Partners LLC boosted its stake in Apple by 0.6% in the second quarter. Berkeley Capital Partners LLC now owns 4,369 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $629,000 after acquiring an additional 26 shares in the last quarter. Hedge funds and other institutional investors own 61.28% of the company’s stock.
Several research firms have issued reports on AAPL. Zacks Investment Research downgraded shares of Apple from a “buy” rating to a “hold” rating in a research note on Friday, January 19th. Mizuho restated a “neutral” rating and issued a $175.00 price objective (up previously from $160.00) on shares of Apple in a research note on Friday, January 19th. Barclays set a $174.00 target price on shares of Apple and gave the stock a “neutral” rating in a research note on Thursday, January 18th. Vetr downgraded shares of Apple from a “buy” rating to a “hold” rating and set a $184.49 target price for the company. in a research note on Tuesday, February 27th. Finally, Bank of America downgraded shares of Apple from a “buy” rating to a “neutral” rating and increased their target price for the stock from $180.00 to $220.00 in a research note on Wednesday, January 17th. Two research analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have assigned a hold rating, thirty-two have issued a buy rating and one has assigned a strong buy rating to the company. Apple has a consensus rating of “Buy” and a consensus target price of $203.15.
In other news, insider Philip W. Schiller sold 69,491 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction dated Tuesday, April 3rd. The shares were sold at an average price of $166.42, for a total value of $11,564,692.22. The transaction was disclosed in a filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is accessible through this hyperlink . Also, SVP Daniel J. Riccio sold 17,375 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction dated Wednesday, April 4th. The stock was sold at an average price of $169.12, for a total transaction of $2,938,460.00. Following the completion of the sale, the senior vice president now directly owns 66,191 shares of the company’s stock, valued at approximately $11,194,221.92. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Insiders have sold a total of 125,988 shares of company stock worth $21,336,201 in the last ninety days. 0.06% of the stock is currently owned by insiders.
Apple stock traded up $0.71 during midday trading on Wednesday, hitting $163.65. 28,289,920 shares of the stock were exchanged, compared to its average volume of 36,220,535. Apple has a 1 year low of $142.20 and a 1 year high of $183.50. The company has a market capitalization of $838,429.94, a price-to-earnings ratio of 17.77, a price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 1.26 and a beta of 1.25. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74, a current ratio of 1.24 and a quick ratio of 1.20.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last released its quarterly earnings results on Thursday, February 1st. The iPhone maker reported $3.89 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, topping the Thomson Reuters’ consensus estimate of $3.82 by $0.07. Apple had a net margin of 21.13% and a return on equity of 37.37%. The firm had revenue of $88.29 billion for the quarter, compared to the consensus estimate of $87.62 billion. During the same quarter in the previous year, the firm posted $3.36 EPS. The firm’s quarterly revenue was up 12.7% on a year-over-year basis. analysts forecast that Apple will post 11.3 earnings per share for the current fiscal year.
